paragraphs: Mentioned at the beginning of Shekalim, chapter 6, as printed with the Babylonian Talmud. Hyman says it should read as in the Jerusalem Talmud edition there: “Rabbi Yudan Antondraya said.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The reference distinguishes Shekalim as printed with the Babylonian Talmud from another Jerusalem Talmud printing. It does not assert a separate Babylonian Shekalim composition.

The entire Guggenheimer Shekalim 6:1 section was read in all fifteen paragraphs. Its ninth paragraph fully names Rabbi Yudan Antondraya (ענתונדרייא), supporting that side of Hyman’s comparison. Abba HaChadiza lacks a locally supported full title and uses R'. Hyman’s “should read” and printing comparison remain attributed; the printing with the Bavli was not freshly collated. The existing note distinguishing printing context from a separate Bavli composition remains verbatim.
